name: Goldman Sachs
summary: Goldman Sachs interviews usually test problem solving, attention to detail and why you want the specific division, with behavioural questions that reflect its core values of partnership, client service, integrity and excellence. For campus roles, candidates commonly report a recorded video interview and, for engineering, an online coding assessment, followed by a final round of several back-to-back interviews.
rounds: Technical interviews: data structures, problem solving
'Superday': several back-to-back interviews including behavioral and fit

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked under real pressure. What did you do?
covers: What made it high pressure: the deadline, the stakes, who was relying on you
How you prioritised and kept the quality up
The result, and what you'd keep or change about how you handled it

questions.text: Why Goldman Sachs, and why this division?
covers: What the division does and who its clients are, in a sentence
Why that work suits your skills and interests, with an example
Something specific about Goldman Sachs you learnt from its people, events or publications

questions.text: Tell me about a mistake you caught before it reached anyone else.
covers: What the mistake was and what it would have cost if missed
How you caught it: the check or habit that found it
What you changed so it wouldn't happen again

questions.text: Tell me about a time you depended on others to hit a deadline. How did you keep the team on track?
covers: Who did what, and where the risk of delay was
How you communicated and helped others, not only your own part
The outcome and what you learnt about working in a team

questions.text: Tell me about a time you went beyond what a client, user or professor expected.
covers: What they asked for and what they actually needed
The extra step you took and why it was worth it
How they responded, with something concrete

questions.text: Walk me through the three financial statements and how they link together.
covers: Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement, and what each shows
How net income flows into retained earnings and the cash flow statement
An example: how a depreciation charge moves through all three

questions.text: How would you value a company? Explain the main approaches and when you'd prefer each.
covers: Discounted cash flow, comparable companies and past transactions
What drives each: forecasts and discount rate, or market multiples
When each fits, for example a young growth firm versus a stable business

questions.text: If interest rates rise sharply, what happens to bond prices, and why?
covers: Prices fall, because existing fixed payments are worth less when new bonds pay more
Longer-dated bonds move more than short-dated ones
A quick note on who gains or loses: investors, borrowers, banks

questions.text: Pitch me a company or stock you follow. What's your view, and what would change your mind?
covers: What the company does and how it makes money, in two sentences
Two or three reasons for your view, with numbers where you have them
The main risk and the signal that would make you change your view

questions.text: Tell me about a recent market move or deal you followed. Why did it happen, and who did it affect?
covers: A specific, recent event described accurately
The main cause in plain words
What it means for clients such as companies, investors or the firm's businesses

questions.text: How would you design a system that shows traders live prices for thousands of instruments with very little delay?
covers: Clarifying scale, update rate and how fresh prices must be
Streaming updates from market feeds through a fast in-memory layer to screens, sending only changes
Handling bursts, slow clients and a feed going down

questions.text: Explain the difference between a process and a thread, and a problem you've seen from shared state.
covers: Processes have separate memory; threads share memory within a process
A race condition or deadlock example and how it showed up
How you fixed or would fix it: locks, immutable data or message passing

questions.text: You roll two fair dice. What's the chance the total is at least 10? Talk me through it.
covers: Counting outcomes: 36 equally likely pairs
Totals of 10, 11 and 12 come from 3, 2 and 1 pairs, so 6 in all
The answer, 6 out of 36 or one in six, stated clearly

questions.text: Where do you see yourself in five years, and how does this role get you there?
covers: A realistic goal linked to this division
The skills you expect to build in the role
Commitment to learning the job well first

tips: Expect probability and puzzle questions alongside coding.
Know why this division specifically, not just why finance.
For the recorded video interview, practise answering to a camera in a set time: a one-line answer first, then one example.
For engineering roles, practise explaining your approach to a coding problem and its time and space cost out loud before you write code.
Final rounds often mean several short interviews with different people; keep your story about why this division consistent and have a fresh question for each interviewer.
Read the financial news for a few weeks before; be ready to discuss one market move and one company in depth.
